text:
Amy: Seeing ~30% drop in forwarded connections to the edge GPU pool in eu-west1 since ~04:10 UTC. NodePort 31500 is getting RSTs from the node. Anyone else seeing this?
Raj: On it. Any recent infra pushes or NACL changes? @deploy-bot did we deploy anything near 04:05?
deploy-bot: Rollout 2025-06-01T04:05 by Lee to 'edge-ingress' completed (4/4 pods ready).
Lee: I only pushed an ingress routing map for host routing, no NACL touches from my side.
Marcus: From inside the cluster I can hit the service on the node port fine. LB -> node seems to be failing, healthchecks returning 504.
Amy: grabbing tcpdump from edge-proxy-12: ```sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 31500 -c 200``` seeing SYN from LB then ICMP port-unreachable or immediate RSTs intermittently.
Raj: That pattern often means a network ACL or SG is rejecting ephemeral-source-port traffic. Can you paste the node's iptables-save and the Network ACL entries?
Amy: iptables looks unchanged. Pulled NACL: looks like eu-west1-edge-subnet NACL has a DENY TCP 31000-31999 with rule number 100 (higher priority than our broad allow). There are duplicate ACL entries from an old test patch.
Lee: I added a deny for a test window weeks ago and was supposed to remove it after migration — totally my mistake. If the deny rule number is numerically lower (i.e. higher priority) it's shadowing the general allow.
Marcus: That would break LB->node because the LB uses ephemeral source ports that land in that range. Quick remediation?
Raj: Two options: (1) insert a specific ALLOW for the LB CIDR for TCP 31000-31999 with a lower rule number (higher priority), (2) remove the old deny. Safer to add an explicit allow for the LB first, then clean up deny after.
Amy: applying interim change now: adding ALLOW rule #50 for CIDR 10.10.20.0/24 TCP 31000-31999 (LB pool).
deploy-bot: Network ACL acl-0abc entries modified by Raj.
Marcus: seeing connections recover — LB healthchecks green, error rate dropping. p95 latency back to baseline within ~2m :tada:
Lee: I'll open a cleanup PR to remove the stale deny and add a comment documenting ephemeral port ranges. Also adding a safety lint in infra tooling so plan fails if NACL denies broad ephemeral ranges.
Amy: creating incident ticket OPER-2025-042, tagging oncall and scheduling a 30m postmortem sync.
Raj: follow-up action: add Terraform guard + automated plan check for any NACL entry that denies 30000-32767 unless explicitly reviewed.
Amy: thanks all — monitoring for the next hour and then we'll close.
